title: Prove live Linux recovery inspection is non-mutating
description: Add one high-value Linux acceptance boundary for the canonical independent recovery-state inspector. During the existing real ublk/ext4 guest lifecycle, invoke `dwv-recovery-inspect --json` after the first workload is unmounted but before the live `dwv demo disk serve` process is terminated, while that process still owns `recovery.sqlite3.dwv-lock`. Prove the inspector can observe the real workload-advanced SQLite artifact without acquiring writable ownership or mutating the database or lock sidecar. This task does not authorize recovery, repair, migration, clean-state, durability, stable-format, or production-service claims.
design: The likely insertion point is `tools/linux-disk-acceptance/guest.sh` immediately after the first `umount "$mountpoint"` and before `kill -TERM "$server_pid"`; update `tools/linux-disk-acceptance/run.sh` only as needed to build the standalone binary. Snapshot the database bytes and lock-sidecar existence/content before and after. Require a status-0 JSON observation with the canonical command schema, supported classification, experimental format claim, bounded non-null manifest, `next_action=none`, and complete non-authorization statement. JSON-only is sufficient because focused command tests already prove human/JSON equivalence. Before implementation, retrieve current canonical context and create or update the bounded OpenSpec artifacts required by the repository workflow; this Bead is execution state, not semantic authority.
acceptance_criteria: The pickup agent has created or updated and validated any required OpenSpec change before product/evidence edits; the Linux guest builds and invokes `dwv-recovery-inspect` while the service still owns the live recovery lock; the assertion fails if inspection takes writable ownership, depends on the production command path, cannot read the real workload-advanced artifact, changes database bytes, or changes/removes the lock sidecar; exact JSON classification, evidence tier, experimental scope, non-claims, and process status are checked without promoting the observation to authority; the focused Linux acceptance command passes; applicable knowledge, documentation, and OpenSpec gates pass; implementation and evidence links are recorded against the canonical requirement.
notes: Investigation evidence: `SqliteRecoveryStore::inspect` uses the read-only sqlite path and does not call `acquire_lock`; `Fixture::open` and `serve_with_publication` keep the writable recovery owner alive through the guest insertion point. Existing unit/CLI tests already cover all six classifications, renderer equivalence, and ordinary non-mutation; macOS APFS uses `MemoryRecoveryStore`. Do not add this test merely as CLI wiring or duplicate absent/corrupt classification coverage.

The archived OpenSpec change is 2026-08-14-add-bounded-parity-scrub; current authority is openspec/specs/independent-parity-verification/spec.md. Adversarial review identified a valid selected-range evidence gap; added valid sub-range and outside-range corruption tests, duplicate JSON-member rejection, refused human/structured equivalence, deterministic human output, and completed-observation exit-code assertions. Final verifier tests pass.
FUTURE EVALUATION CANDIDATES (not current implementation or a blocker; retained for a future agent to assess):

1. Kani candidate — pure verifier arithmetic and read-outcome decisions. Relevant symbols: crates/dwv-verify/src/independent_parity.rs::parse_descriptor (roughly lines 394-542), ::observe (roughly 814-930), ::read_data_region (760-789), and ::read_parity_region (791-812). If the arithmetic is factored without changing the external contract, consider cfg(kani) proofs for: (a) region tiling is contiguous, non-overlapping, sums exactly to selected length, each region is <= region_size, and count equals ceil(selected_length / region_size), including exact-multiple and remainder cases; (b) checked u64 additions, ceiling division, u64-to-usize conversions, buffer multiplication, and bound acceptance/refusal cannot panic or wrap, including u64::MAX edges; (c) read decisions never synthesize in-range bytes, data zero-extension occurs only beyond declared data length, parity never zero-extends, and unknown/incomplete precedence is conservative. Kani is a poor fit for serde_json rendering, filesystem canonicalization, dev/ino identity, and real I/O fault behavior. Existing repository proof precedent includes cfg(kani) modules in dwv-core/src/topology.rs and dwv-service/src/range.rs. First evaluate whether factoring pure functions is worth the abstraction.

2. Property-testing/fuzzing candidate — descriptor parser boundary. Relevant symbols: reject_duplicate_members and parse_descriptor (independent_parity.rs roughly lines 347-542), with an input harness of &[u8] -> Result that does not open payloads. The repository currently has no proptest, quickcheck, or cargo-fuzz framework, so adding one is optional future work, not an accepted dependency. A structure-aware generator could inject duplicate object keys at top level and nested values; unknown fields, versions, profiles, features, explicit nulls and wrong types; malformed/trailing JSON; path/count/byte/region bounds; and overflow-sized ranges. Properties: deterministic result and reason; no panic; bounded parser/output work; invalid input refuses before payload reads; no payload, parity, descriptor, or recovery-state writes. The deterministic duplicate-version regression test already covers last-key-wins risk; fuzzing is only worthwhile if parser bug yield justifies new tooling/dependency and corpus maintenance.

3. Keep process-boundary cases example-based: human/structured status equivalence, exit-code mapping, symlink/hardlink aliases, non-mutation digests, and output failures are OS/process semantics and are not good Kani targets. A future agent should compare marginal defect-finding value, repository precedent, build cost, and dependency/corpus maintenance before opening either candidate. Current evidence explicitly does not claim arbitrary filesystem read faults or exit-1 output-channel fault injection.

acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec tasks 1.1-2.2 are complete; every operator result uses dwv.operator.v2; current production evidence yields only classifications it proves; no recovery schema, recovery mutation, payload mutation, start authorization, retry, compatibility shim, or C0b/C2 behavior is added.
close_reason: C0a v2 authority model, conservative classifier, renderers, focused tests, and documentation gates are complete.

title: Implement post-gap authority assessment
description: Implement the bounded C0a operator capability defined by OpenSpec change add-post-gap-authority-assessment. The assessment inspects a candidate array after a custody gap, reports authority and uncertainty without mutation, and grants no publication, repair, protection, continuity, or recovery authorization.
design: OpenSpec change add-post-gap-authority-assessment owns required behavior. Reuse current operator-recovery observation, identity, recovery-state, evidence, and bounded-output owners. Do not implement C0b, publication, writes, repair, historical recovery, or mutation.
acceptance_criteria: All child implementation and evidence Beads are closed; the OpenSpec change acceptance scenarios pass; the campaign records the completed implementation/evidence anchors without expanding beyond U01.
close_reason: C0a implementation, evidence, canonical OpenSpec archive, and campaign closure are complete.

title: Separate planning scan capacity bound
description: The readiness planning-nomenclature scan currently reuses max_units=512 for the entire tracked-file path list, so a 519-file repository fails before scanning. Separate the planning path capacity from semantic packet limits without changing fail-closed behavior or silently skipping files.
design: Add a dedicated finite planning path bound, preserve max_units for semantic units and packet/reference limits, report a planning-specific bound error, and add focused regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Readiness no longer fails solely because this repository has 519 tracked paths; semantic max_units remains unchanged; a planning path overflow still fails closed with a planning-specific error; focused xtask tests and docs/OpenSpec checks pass.
notes: Implemented max_planning_scan_paths=2048 in xtask Bounds; planning scanner now fails closed with planning_scan_path_bound_exceeded instead of consuming max_units. Added independent-capacity regression. Passed focused planning tests, readiness, docs check, OpenSpec validation (27/27), and semantic context/affected tests. Full cargo test -p xtask has one unrelated pre-existing failure: architecture catalog test expects only v0.6-v0.8 while current v0.9 candidate documents are present. cargo fmt --check also remains blocked by pre-existing independent_parity.rs formatting drift.
close_reason: Implemented and verified; bounded planning scan capacity is independent from semantic-unit limits.

title: Refresh active Linux C0a acceptance evidence
description: Regenerate the live Linux acceptance artifact after the dwv.operator.v2 cutover. Keep historical M9 v1 records unchanged, but update the active runner and retained evidence together so schema, authority fields, and publication assertions match the current canonical operator contract.
design: Use the current tools/linux-disk-acceptance runner and current operator result contract; do not reinterpret the archived M9 evidence or add a v1 compatibility alias.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh bounded Linux acceptance run produces verification/linux-ublk-ext4-acceptance.json with dwv.operator.v2 and the complete current production-start result, and the runner's jq assertion accepts it; historical docs/verification/m9.md remains explicitly historical.
notes: Claimed for this repair. The active Linux runner now asserts dwv.operator.v2, and the human renderer now exposes schema, exact basis ranges, and bounded verification-region findings. A fresh Linux guest run is still required to regenerate verification/linux-ublk-ext4-acceptance.json; historical M9 v1 evidence remains unchanged.
close_reason: Fresh bounded acceptance run regenerated the active dwv.operator.v2 artifact and traces; historical M9 v1 evidence remains unchanged.

title: Reconcile session-close fence supersession
description: Define when an exact global close-session fence over a closed mutation set may supersede per-write fence evidence without weakening integrity, claim, or uncertainty semantics.
design: Compose the durable writable-session begin/close owner rather than inventing a fence-local shutdown policy. Supersession requires quiescence, exact store/range/generation coverage, all backend children terminal/reconciled, and atomic handoff.
acceptance_criteria: The U11 session owner and fence owner agree on closed-set admission, exact close evidence, crash/restart outcomes, claim dependencies, and which per-write certificates remain live; no service implementation starts before canonical ownership exists.

title: Define rebuild claim-material handoff
description: Define when rebuild source evidence and the detailed record may stop supporting current or advertised recovery claims after verified promotion.
design: Compose A13/A14/U14 preservation with operation-local rebuild authority. Separate current recovery authority from optional audit history, tombstones, retention duration, and identifier reuse.
acceptance_criteria: The claim owner states preserve narrow retire outcomes for every selected claim; unresolved audit retention, tombstone, and identifier-reuse choices are explicit human decisions and cannot silently block or authorize current recovery.

title: Define rebuild block cancel and rollback dispositions
description: Define operator-visible durable outcomes for rebuild verification failure, blocked work, cancellation, refusal, rollback, and abandoned replacement targets; current code has a Blocked value but no canonical transition or recovery mutation.
design: Preserve source topology and replacement bytes until the selected owner permits disposal. Keep cancellation distinct from rollback and from operation abandonment; no automatic record eviction.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical semantics define every terminal and resumable disposition, ownership release, replacement disposal, and crash/restart behavior; required human approval is recorded before operator-visible recovery behavior changes.

title: Govern bounded service-lifetime invariant
description: After operation-local capacity rules are coherent, reconcile and govern the narrowed v0.9 A17 rule that normal supported operation cannot consume hidden irreversible lifetime allowances.
design: Refine existing canonical owners; do not create standalone generic lifecycle, GC, or invariant registries. Preserve explicit finite exhaustion where mathematically unavoidable. Require valid current constrains links and separately attributable human review before architecture activation.
acceptance_criteria: A17 wording is safe, complete, and linked to current owners; no duplicate policy owner exists; all affected requirement fingerprints are individually reviewed; architecture activation remains a separate human-approved action.

title: Reconcile recovery-manifest representability
description: After retained fence and rebuild liveness is settled, define the SQLite adapter admission rule that every supported portable recovery snapshot must fit the selected count and serialized-size profile before dependent mutation.
design: The 16 MiB limit is adapter conformance, not a second product invariant or license to truncate or delete live records. Select explicit unsupported or migration outcomes when representation cannot be guaranteed.
acceptance_criteria: Current semantic liveness inputs are known; adapter admission, migration/refusal, and crash behavior are canonicalized and evidenced without truncation or silent claim loss.

title: Reconcile finite identity reset domains
description: Define bounded exhaustion and safe reset-domain behavior for finite slot/tag generations and other reusable correctness identities without same-process rollover ambiguity or reuse while references survive.
design: Keep operation-local counter owners. Require explicit exhaustion before mutation and a new disambiguating namespace or proof all old channels and references are fenced and reconciled before reset. Do not require infinite counters or one universal identity framework.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical owners state refusal and reset conditions for each selected identity family, deterministic evidence covers stale-reference rejection and crash/restart boundaries, and unrelated RecoveryGeneration or TopologyEpoch policy is not widened.

title: Canonicalize independent parity verifier
description: Apply OpenSpec tasks 3.1-3.3 after implementation and focused evidence. Verify the change, review affected owners individually, archive only after all contracts pass, link the executable and evidence to req.independent-parity-verification.standalone-equation-verification-is-bounded-read-only-and-non-authorizing, update the temporary campaign's C8b/U26b split and remaining open IDs, export shared tracker state if required, and close the feature last.
design: Treat the campaign and Beads as temporary execution state; the archived OpenSpec is the only authority transition. Do not modify current specs directly, archive around failed evidence, close C8a/U26a or U11, start U26b remainder, claim stable format, or broaden into repair, migration, recovery, publication, shutdown, or history/retention.
acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec verification finds no incomplete task or contract drift; archive produces the new canonical capability; implementation/evidence links and individual dependent reviews are recorded; documentation gates and focused evidence pass when run by the implementation owner; campaign records current-versus-target posture honestly and preserves all adjacent unresolved/deferred rows; exported viewer state is current and the parent feature can close only after this Bead.
close_reason: Verified proposal, delta, design, focused evidence, canonical owner review, docs check/build; archived as openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-14-add-bounded-parity-scrub with current requirement linked to implementation and evidence.

title: Verify archive and canonicalize shutdown
description: Apply OpenSpec tasks 3.1-4.3 after implementation and evidence. Run focused checks and strict OpenSpec verification, archive only after all contracts pass, add canonical implementation/evidence links, review every affected dependent individually, run knowledge/documentation gates, update U11/C1-C2 campaign anchors without claiming premature authority, export viewer JSONL, and close the feature last.
design: Use openspec-verify-change before openspec-archive-change. Keep the campaign temporary and the OpenSpec archive as the only authority transition. Do not archive around failed evidence, modify current specs directly, close U02/C2/U26b/U35 or the recovery-inspection chain, or run a global normalization pass.
acceptance_criteria: The change verifies with no incomplete task or contract drift and is archived; the portable owner and Linux refinement have canonical implementation/evidence links; all affected reviewed states are resolved individually; readiness, docs check, and docs build pass; campaign records target/current posture and remaining open IDs honestly; exported .beads/issues.jsonl and bv show the feature-to-implementation-to-evidence-to-canonicalization chain closed in order.

title: Clarify knowledge readiness timing
description: The DiskWeave knowledge skill currently reads like readiness is mandatory before every product-related task, although readiness only affects work that relies on derived knowledge state or establishes a change-boundary baseline. Clarify the SDLC timing without changing canonical product semantics.
acceptance_criteria: The skill distinguishes ordinary read-only research from baseline readiness checks, keeps one readiness call per applicable change boundary, and retains docs check as the completion impact gate.
close_reason: Clarified readiness as a derived-knowledge change-boundary baseline gate; no OpenSpec change required because the canonical workflow requirement delegates concrete readiness timing to trusted skill instructions.

title: Canonicalize independent recovery inspection
description: Apply OpenSpec tasks 3.2 through 3.3 after implementation evidence passes. Verify and archive add-independent-recovery-state-inspection, add canonical implementation/evidence links, resolve reviewed-requirement state, update U26/C8 campaign anchors, run repository documentation gates, export Beads state for bv, and close the feature.
design: Use openspec-verify-change before openspec-archive-change. Treat the campaign and Beads as execution state, not semantic authority. Do not archive around failed evidence, declare stable format, expand into equation verification/parity construction/candidate export/recovery-plan explanation, or start another capability.
acceptance_criteria: The OpenSpec change verifies with no incomplete task or contract drift and is archived; the new main spec is canonical and linked to implementation/evidence; knowledge readiness, docs check, docs build, strict OpenSpec validation, and bd lint pass; campaign U26/C8 records final durable anchors without closing U27; bv reports the completed chain closed after JSONL export.
close_reason: Canonical requirement archived and linked to implementation and evidence; reviewed-requirement gate, strict OpenSpec validation, documentation gates, campaign update, and Bead lint pass.

title: Canonicalize verified C0a semantics
description: After dwv-roy.1 and dwv-roy.2 complete, verify add-post-gap-authority-assessment against its artifacts, archive the OpenSpec change so the modified operator-recovery requirement becomes current canonical authority, and update U01/C0a campaign state with the final requirement, implementation, evidence, and Bead anchors.
design: Use openspec-verify-change before openspec-archive-change. Treat the campaign as temporary execution state, not authority. Do not close or archive around failed evidence or unresolved semantic review.
acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec verification finds no incomplete task or contract drift; the change is archived; current operator-recovery semantics contain the C0a requirement; the campaign marks U01 canonicalized with durable anchors but does not advance C0b/C2; the parent feature can close.
close_reason: Verified and archived C0a OpenSpec change; canonical requirement synced and campaign updated with implementation/evidence anchors.

title: Audit operation-specific lifecycle coverage for U12
description: Resolve the retained v0.8 U12 intent by checking rollover, scrub, checksum, rebuild, mover, and other long-running operations for stable identity, cancellation, resume, and persisted correctness-cursor coverage.
design: Prefer composition of operation-specific owners. Add no umbrella owner merely for symmetry; missing independent predicates remain separate work.
acceptance_criteria: Each relevant operation has a canonical owner or explicit durable deferral for identity, cancellation, resume, and cursor semantics; any real gap becomes a bounded follow-up Bead; campaign U12 receives a terminal disposition.
